solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One responsible for housekeeping as Dick Grayson's working

parts.note: Dick Grayson is the first Robin, Batman's sidekick; 'Dick Grayson's' is read as Robin's
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps house, apparently while Batman's young sidekick is busy elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housekeeping' is the novel by Marilynne Robinson, so the one responsible for it is its author, not a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilynne Robinson wrote the 1980 novel Housekeeping, so she is literally the person responsible for it.

clue.text: He died lifting gold in lines in a novel

indicators.note: in places the death note and the metal inside the railway

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway lines
OB is short for obiit, Latin for 'he died', seen on gravestones

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue reads the heraldic word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A man in a novel dies while hoisting gold along a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He died' looks like the hero's fate; it is the gravestone abbreviation, with OR turned upwards after it, inside RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rob Roy is Walter Scott's 1817 novel about the Highland outlaw Rob Roy MacGregor.

clue.text: Admiral and oarsman supporting Munro?

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means standing underneath, so this part goes second

parts.note: a Munro is a Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet, and many are called Ben something; the question mark flags this definition by example
the bow is the rower nearest the front of the boat

explanation.surface: A naval officer and a rower backing a writer named Munro, perhaps Saki.
explanation.walkthrough: Munro looks like a surname (Saki was H.H. Munro), but it is a Scottish peak, and a Scottish mountain is a ben.
explanation.definitionFit: John Benbow was a celebrated English admiral of the late seventeenth century, remembered in the ballad Admiral Benbow.

clue.text: A queen uses it on marshland without it flipping over

indicators.note: flipping over turns the whole string upside down, so in a down clue it reads backwards

parts.note: the second it is placed outside, at the front of the rest
taken as written
RE means on, as in 're your letter'
a fen is low marshy ground, as in the Fens of eastern England

explanation.surface: A queen employs something on boggy ground, taking care that it does not turn over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without it' places a second IT outside IT RE FEN; flipping the whole string gives the Egyptian queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was the Egyptian queen, wife of the pharaoh Akhenaten, famous from her painted bust in Berlin.

clue.text: A tale of my landlord's rent, my tailor told

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, so the words that follow are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: My tailor passed on a story about my landlord and the rent he charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money owed to the landlord, but it is the past participle of rend: torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Mortality is one of Scott's novels published in the series called Tales of My Landlord.

clue.text: He sang about the Empire Falls writer losing heart

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: losing its heart means the writer's name drops its central letter

parts.note: Richard Russo wrote the Pulitzer-winning novel Empire Falls

explanation.surface: Someone sang about the author of Empire Falls, a man who had lost heart.
explanation.walkthrough: RUSSO has five letters, so its heart is the middle S; 'losing heart' leaves RUSO.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Caruso was the celebrated Italian operatic tenor, so he is a man who sang.

clue.text: Isolated, like Hamlet for example

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: being a role an actor plays

explanation.surface: Hamlet is the classic example of a man cut off from everyone around him.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words to get the second sense: Hamlet is a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means separated or alone, and Hamlet is a part in the theatrical sense, a role.

clue.text: A purist's not right in the head

indicators.note: not right means wrong or disordered, so the letters before it are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
the S of the possessive joins the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone obsessed with purity is a bit mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right in the head' reads as one phrase for insanity; it splits into the anagram signal and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstairs is a colloquial word for the mind or brain, as in 'not much going on upstairs'.

clue.text: Old lover who crossed a flower and shrub

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero; a flower is something that flows, a river or strait

explanation.surface: An old flame who crossbred a flower with a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossed' suggests plant breeding and 'flower' a bloom; in crossword language a flower is a river, and Leander swam across the Hellespont.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is a poisonous evergreen Mediterranean shrub with pink or white flowers.

clue.text: Genuine papers found by a female in Ilium?

indicators.note: in places the papers and the woman inside the body part that follows

parts.note: the ilium is the large bone of the pelvis; the question mark flags the trick, since Ilium is also Troy
taken as written
F is the standard abbreviation for female
identity papers are ID

explanation.surface: Authentic documents discovered with a woman in ancient Troy, the city Homer calls Ilium.
explanation.walkthrough: Ilium is the classical name for Troy, which suits a literary puzzle, but the question mark points to the other ilium, part of the pelvis.
explanation.definitionFit: Bona fide is Latin for 'in good faith' and is used in English to mean real or authentic.

clue.text: Bingley's friend talked of one to Alan Fairford

indicators.note: something talked of is heard spoken, so it is the sound of the name that counts

parts.note: in Pride and Prejudice, Mr Darcy is Mr Bingley's close friend

explanation.surface: Someone discussing Jane Austen's Mr Darcy with a character from a Walter Scott novel.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scott's Redgauntlet, Darsie Latimer is the dearest friend of the young lawyer Alan Fairford; their letters open the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Darsie Latimer is Alan Fairford's closest companion in Redgauntlet, so he is 'one' (a friend) to him.

clue.text: Resists clue being "Posters of the sea and land"

definitions.text: Posters of the sea and land

indicators.note: calling the printed word a clue tells us it is the outcome of a rearrangement, which the answer itself describes

parts.note: the printed word is what the second half of the answer becomes when its letters are reshuffled
read as 'being made weird': the first word of the answer is the instruction that produced the printed word

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to accept a clue quoting a line about messengers travelling over sea and land.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, 'sisters' made weird, and it produces the clue word Resists.
explanation.definitionFit: In Macbeth the witches call themselves 'The weird sisters, hand in hand, Posters of the sea and land', posters meaning swift travellers.

clue.text: Quality of chrysanthemums in Lawrence's bouquet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the first word of the title of D.H. Lawrence's short story about chrysanthemums
second meaning: the smell of a wine

explanation.surface: Describing the scent of a bunch of chrysanthemums in a D.H. Lawrence story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' looks like a bunch of flowers, completing the chrysanthemum picture, but it is the wine-taster's word for smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence's story is titled Odour of Chrysanthemums, and a wine's bouquet is its characteristic smell or aroma.

clue.text: Plain Maugham story used in school too much?

parts.note: plain, as in open and obvious
Rain is Somerset Maugham's famous short story about Sadie Thompson

explanation.surface: A simple Maugham story being taught in classrooms rather too often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' reads as a noun but is the verb, to train; the question mark admits the definition is a loose paraphrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To school is to train or drill, so to school someone too much is to train them excessively.

clue.text: Miss Meeber's evil, but not in a horror story

indicators.note: but not in tells us to take a two-letter word out of the adjective

parts.note: sinister means evil or menacing
the word in is the part removed
Carrie is Stephen King's first published novel, a horror story

explanation.surface: A woman named Meeber has a wicked side, though it does not belong in a horror story.
explanation.walkthrough: Caroline Meeber is the heroine of Theodore Dreiser's novel, so the definition 'Miss Meeber's' means the book that is hers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreiser's 1900 novel Sister Carrie tells the story of Caroline 'Carrie' Meeber, so the book belongs to her.

clue.text: Pushkin's old lover in The Eagle?

indicators.note: in places the former partner inside the spacecraft named next

parts.note: the Eagle was the Apollo 11 lunar module, a lander; the question mark marks the example
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A former love of the Russian poet, appearing in a work called The Eagle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Eagle has landed' were the first words from the Moon: the Eagle was a lander, so read it as A LANDER with EX inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushkin's first name was Alexander, so 'Pushkin's' given name is the answer.

clue.text: What nanny might give you next

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: what a nanny goat might do to you with her horns

explanation.surface: Wondering what a children's nanny might hand out to you next.
explanation.walkthrough: The nanny here is not a childminder but a female goat, and goats butt.
explanation.definitionFit: Abutting means bordering on or adjacent, so a house abutting yours is next door.

clue.text: Article, say, by a writer returning Fenton's love

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the preceding letters are read in the opposite order

parts.note: EG, for example, is another way of saying 'say'
taken as written
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece in which an author writes back to a man called Fenton about his love life.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Merry Wives of Windsor, the young gentleman Fenton woos and finally marries Anne Page.

clue.text: Burns's girl's been lonely and is out of sorts

indicators.note: out of sorts means upset and disordered, so the letters before it are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The poet's sweetheart has been lonely and feels unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonnie Lesley is a 1792 song by Robert Burns praising Lesley Baillie, a girl he admired.

clue.text: This writer's regularly dissented about Polynices' sister

indicators.note: about means the kept letters wrap around the writer
regularly means at even intervals, so only every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
the setter refers to himself as this writer, meaning me

explanation.surface: An author admits to having repeatedly disagreed about Antigone's sister.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is', a link; the kept letters of dissented go around ME.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Ismene is the daughter of Oedipus, sister of Antigone, Eteocles and Polynices.

clue.text: Shows some critics are potty about

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the concealed letters are read backwards
some means a part of the following words, so the answer lies within them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of critics through are into the start of potty

explanation.surface: Certain reviewers are crazy about some theatre productions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows' could be a verb meaning displays; it is the noun, stage productions.
explanation.definitionFit: Operas are staged musical dramas, a kind of theatrical show.

clue.text: He mocked nobles taking over from other positions

indicators.note: taking the cricket term from the phrase means removing it from the letters

parts.note: positions are sites
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone who ridiculed aristocrats as they displaced others from their posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking over from' looks like one phrase meaning replacing; it splits into taking O from OTHER SITES.
explanation.definitionFit: Thersites is the foul-mouthed soldier who jeers at Agamemnon and Achilles in the Iliad and Troilus and Cressida.

clue.text: Writer's block providing time for church

indicators.note: providing one thing for another means swapping it in where the other stood

parts.note: to scotch is to block or thwart a plan; a scotch is also a wedge that blocks a wheel
T is the abbreviation for time
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Writer's block, the familiar affliction, apparently cured by setting aside time for church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's block' is a phrase every reader recognises, but it splits: the definition is Writer, and block is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Scott was the Scottish novelist and poet who wrote Waverley, Ivanhoe and Rob Roy.

clue.text: Sit back to follow a storyteller

indicators.note: to follow means this part comes after the article in the answer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for sit in the opposite direction

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: An instruction to lean back and listen to someone telling tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is the ancient Greek teller of fables such as The Tortoise and the Hare.

clue.text: A Chekhov play's hero of 22, after he's lifted to victory

indicators.note: lifted in the sense of removed: the two letters of the word he are taken out of the hero's name, wherever they sit

parts.note: 22-down is SCOTT, and Ivanhoe is the hero of his novel of that name

explanation.surface: A literary question about which Chekhov hero is carried to triumph on others' shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's lifted' removes H and E from IVANHOE; they are not side by side, as the O between them stays, so HOE shrinks to O. 22-down is SCOTT, author of Ivanhoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanov is Chekhov's first full-length drama, named after its troubled central character.

clue.text: Aim to tackle what goes on at the top

definitions.text: what goes on at the top

parts.note: to aim for somewhere is to head for it
tackle is equipment, as in fishing tackle, which is gear

explanation.surface: Sporting advice: aim to tackle whatever is going on at the top of the league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What goes on at the top' reads as events at the summit; it means what is put on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Headgear is a hat or helmet, something put on, or worn, at the top of the body.

clue.text: Students might read this novel without expectation

indicators.note: without means lacking, so one word of the title is dropped

parts.note: a novel: Dickens's Great Expectations
the word is the part removed

explanation.surface: Students may read a certain novel without expecting much from it.
explanation.walkthrough: Greats is the Oxford name for the Classics degree course (Literae Humaniores), which students 'read' in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford, students read Greats, the final honours course in classics and philosophy.

clue.text: When to use art forged for a Titan

parts.note: as in 'as I left', meaning when

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new shape, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on when to employ counterfeit art to impress a giant of the industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forged' sits after the fodder it acts on: the letters of use art are rearranged and placed after AS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Astraeus is a Titan of the dusk and the stars, father of the four winds.
